title: A Message Passing Neural Network Space for Better Capturing Data-dependent Receptive Fields

problem.claim: MPNNs learn node representations from a node's receptive field, but conventional MPNNs cannot handle the variant receptive fields required across different graphs.

gap.claim: Existing upgraded methods use a common solution across graphs and therefore fail to capture how different graph properties affect receptive fields.

contributions.claim: The authors propose MpnnDRF, an MPNN space that dynamically designs suitable MPNNs for the receptive field of a given graph.
The authors investigate existing MPNN designs, identify design dimensions, incorporate these and useful designs into a search space, and formulate a search framework.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe MpnnDRF and its search space as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: In the empirical study, MpnnDRF shows strong robustness to an increased receptive field and can learn node representations from a larger perceptual field.
The authors report that MpnnDRF consistently achieves outstanding performance on benchmark node and graph classification tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: MPNNs learn node representations based on node receptive fields.
Conventional MPNNs cannot handle variant receptive fields across graphs, while existing upgrades use a common solution that overlooks graph-specific properties.
MpnnDRF dynamically designs suitable MPNNs for each graph; the authors develop design dimensions, a search space, and a search framework.
The authors report robustness to increased receptive fields and strong benchmark classification performance.

source_observation.claim: A common MPNN design may fail to account for graph-specific effects on receptive fields.

interpretation.claim: Model architecture selection may need to depend on properties of the input graph rather than rely on one universal design.

application.claim: For graph-learning systems, consider data-dependent architecture search when receptive-field requirements vary across graphs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when a common architecture is sufficient or which graph properties determine the required receptive field.

unknowns: No datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results are specified.
The design dimensions, search procedure, and computational costs are unspecified.
The graph properties used for data-dependent design are unspecified.
No limitations or failure cases are reported.
